cases.answer: Set the parking brake; select Park or Neutral for an automatic, or fully depress the clutch and select Neutral for a manual vehicle. Turn off unneeded lights and accessories, make one controlled start attempt, and listen for unusual noises. Observe whether the dash lights normally or dims, whether there is a click, whether the engine cranks, and whether it starts then stops; report those observations instead of guessing a diagnosis. Use the vehicle owner's manual for immobilizer, key, jump-start, and model-specific steps; treat EV and hybrid propulsion systems as model-specific and do not touch orange high-voltage components.
Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute. Above 6,500 feet (about 1,980 metres), boil for 3 minutes.

Stop as soon as landmarks, trail, or position stop matching expectations. Mark the spot without damaging the environment and record time and direction of travel. Review the last certain point, recent turns, terrain, distance, and elevation before moving.
Apply immediate firm pressure to the wound with a clean cloth or gauze. Do not loosen the tourniquet after application; obtain emergency evacuation as quickly as possible.

Move out of wind and wet, replace wet clothing, and insulate above and below. Warm the chest, neck, armpits, and groin with wrapped warm packs or shared body heat. Protect frostbitten tissue from pressure and refreezing; evacuate serious cases.

Leave ridges, peaks, open water, and isolated tall objects immediately. If no safe building or vehicle exists, spread a group apart and move toward lower terrain away from water and tall isolated trees. Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before leaving safe shelter.

Estimate likely rescue time, weather, health, daylight, and food already available. Choose only methods with a high chance of return and low injury risk. Stop if gathering consumes water, warmth, navigation certainty, or signaling time. Protect existing calories and use them to support warmth, decisions, and necessary work.

Secure line to a purpose-made rod or handline, attach a suitable hook and any float or weight the gear requires, add locally legal bait, and keep the line attended. Present the bait from a stable bank near cover or a current edge without wading, swimming, climbing, or reaching over unstable ground; retrieve steadily and land the fish without entering the water. Keep hands, tools, and ready-to-eat food away from raw fish contamination, and cook retained fish to 145 °F at the thickest part when a food thermometer is available. Fish only where legal and only if you have suitable gear and safe access to the bank.

Use carried food or other lower-risk options first. Treat look-alike species, mushrooms, berries, roots, and water plants as unknown unless already known with certainty. Keep unknown material away from children and food-preparation surfaces. Do not eat unfamiliar animals, shellfish, insects, or plants merely because another animal ate them.
